01. 1.
This matter is taken up through hybrid arrangement (virtual/physical) mode.

2. The Petitioners, by filing this writ petition has invoked the jurisdiction of this Court under Article 226 and 227 of the Constitution of India seeking issuance of a writ of mandamus or any other writ or order directing the Opposite Parties to identify the Petitioners as "Displaced Families" and to provide them Rehabilitation & Resettlement benefits under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
3. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and learned Additional Standing Counsel.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. Keeping in view the submissions made, we have gone through the averments taken in the writ petition as also the documents annexed thereto.

5. It reveals that pursuant to the order dated 20.03.2023 passed by this Court in W.P.(C) No.6872 of Prasant Kumar Naik & Others vs ) The Collector & District Magistrate on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39810653/
1 2023, the representation of the Petitioners on the above score has been dealt with by the Collector &
District Magistrate.

entities.text: W.P.(C) No.6872 of Prasant Kumar Naik & Others vs ) The Collector & District Magistrate on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Angul in Misc. Case No.33 of 2023.

The Collector and District Magistrate, Angul in its order dated 10.01.2024 having gone through all the relevant reports as also the documents and discussing all those in great detail assigning very good reasons as reflected in the order has arrived at a conclusion that the Petitioners are not entitled to get any Rehabilitation and Resettlement benefits towards acquisition of their lands as per the Odisha Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy,
2006 which was then in place
It has been held that neither the Petitioners nor his family are falling within the definition of Displaced Persons or Family as per the said Policy.

That being so, since the Petitioners now dispute the factual findings arrived at by the Collector in holding them as not entitled to the benefits under the Odisha Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy, 2006, the said arena not being permissible to be gone into in this proceeding, we are hereby dismiss the writ petition.
Issue urgent certified copy as per rules.

(D. Dash), Judge (V. Narasingh) Judge H Signed by: HIMANSU SEKHAR DASH Prasant Kumar Naik & Others vs ) The Collector & District Magistrate on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39810653/
